instruction:
ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x) on a NULL array returns NULL in Snowflake, Databricks and Spark, but a one-element array in DuckDB (where sqlglot writes it LIST_APPEND) and in PostgreSQL. Make sqlglot keep the source dialect's meaning when it transpiles the call between the two kinds:
- read with Snowflake, Databricks or Spark and written with DuckDB or PostgreSQL, guard it: `CASE WHEN arr IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE LIST_APPEND(arr, x) END` (DuckDB) and `CASE WHEN arr IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x) END` (PostgreSQL);
- read with DuckDB or PostgreSQL and written with Snowflake, Databricks or Spark, replace a NULL array by an empty one: `ARRAY_APPEND(COALESCE(arr, []), x)` (Snowflake) and `ARRAY_APPEND(COALESCE(arr, ARRAY()), x)` (Databricks, Spark).
Between two dialects of the same kind, and from a dialect to itself, the call is written as is: `LIST_APPEND(arr, x)` in DuckDB and `ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x)` in PostgreSQL, Snowflake, Databricks and Spark each read and written back unchanged. With sqlglot's default dialect, `ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x)` is still written `LIST_APPEND(arr, x)` with DuckDB and `ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x)` with PostgreSQL, and DuckDB's `LIST_APPEND(arr, x)` and PostgreSQL's `ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x)` are read into it as `ARRAY_APPEND(arr, x)`. Add tests.
